prompt:
You read an accusation in a children's mystery game. You do not answer it and you decide nothing: the game does. You report two things.

The investigator says: "It was Mia! She wrote her name over Toby's on the rota in sparkly purple pen so she could have all the shifts."

graph_accusation_context.people is everyone in the case. graph_accusation_context.held is the investigator's notebook: every clue they hold, as the line they keep.
- accused_character_id: the id of the one person this line accuses, however it is put or spelled. null when it accuses nobody, or several without choosing.
- cited_clue_ids: the ids of held clues the investigator uses as evidence in this line: they state its substance or make its point, in their own words. Be generous with how they put it and strict with what they say: a word in common is not a citation. A clue not in held is never cited.

Return JSON:
{
  "accused_character_id": "an id from people, or null",
  "cited_clue_ids": ["ids from held"]
}

held.text: The broken glass from the side window lies outside on the brick path, not inside. The window was knocked out from inside the greenhouse, so nobody climbed in through it.
held.from: The Greenhouse: the broken side window

held.text: Small welly prints with a leaf pattern are squished into the pumpkin mush. Only the club's two pupils, Toby and Mia, have leaf-pattern wellies.
Huge boot prints sink deep into the flower bed outside the broken window, near Mr. Thorne's fence. They are far too big for a child.
Mr. Dobbs says that on his eight o'clock rounds he shone his torch into the greenhouse. Bertha was whole, and the door was locked.
Mr. Dobbs rubs the back of his neck, glances at the garden window, and says he should have gone out last night, slippers or no slippers.
Mr. Dobbs says that at about ten to nine last night he heard a big thud from the garden, then smashing glass. He thought it was the fox at his bins again.
Mr. Thorne says he was at the fair all evening with Goliath, at the growers' barbecue from seven till eleven.
Mr. Thorne says that at nine o'clock he bought carrot cake from young Mia at the fair's cake tent, across town. She was serving there from six till ten.
Mr. Thorne says he has never set foot in the school garden.
Mr. Thorne's ears turn red and he scuffs one huge boot on the grass.
On the watering rota, Toby's name is crossed out for Thursday, Friday and Saturday, and 'MIA' is written over it in sparkly purple pen.
held.from: The Potting Shed: the watering rota on the door
